messages:
anya: Heads up — I just switched orgs in Console and saw the "Create project" button while signed in as a Viewer. Screenshot: https://files.redwood/test/edge-btn.png
chris: whoa that shouldn't happen. is this reproable for you every time?
anya: yep, steps: 1) org A (viewer) -> 2) quick org switch to org B -> 3) Create project button appears in header. Happens on Chrome + incognito.
sara: any logs on the backend when you click it? server should deny on create-project POST.
anya: clicked it to test — UI shows modal then API returns 403 when submitting. but button visible is the issue.
kevin: sounds like UI gating check is client-only in some code path. I remember a recent role mapping change where legacy role flags were merged during org switch.
sara: digging: console-web/src/components/Header/ProjectCreateButton.tsx has `if (user.permissions.includes('project:create')) show` and the permissions get recomputed from local cache on org change. cache invalidation race maybe.
chris: reproduce + logs please, and include console warnings. also tag oncall? @sec-bot can you triage severity?
sec-bot: [auto] Security triage requested by chris for UI exposure of privileged action. Initial severity: P2. Notes: no successful backend creation observed; audit log entry absent for attempted UI click.
kevin: audit log bit odd — when I looked at admin/audit/events there was no entry for the UI click, only a failed POST 403 (console-api). KMS audit log shows no key-access around that time.
anya: timeline: 11:42:12 UI shows button, 11:42:35 POST /projects -> 403, 11:42:36 client shows error. Audit table: empty for project:create attempts.
sara: that implies the UI click isn't being recorded by our client-side analytics or our api-gateway isn't logging the preflight. Could be a dropped event due to new proxy config.
chris: more concerning: if a support-privilege elevation flow occurred earlier for the same org, the role merge might leave a residual permission flag in the client cache. kevin, can you grep session-store for sticky flags?
kevin: grep shows legacy mapping code in rbac-service v3.2.4: `mergedRoles = union(session.cachedRoles, org.roles)` — we don't clear cachedRoles on org switch if session.isTransient === true. That's the bug.
sara: ok that explains button visibility. mitigation: update client to always invalidate cachedRoles on org switch + add server-side double-check to hide privileged UI elements based on fresh /whoami fetch.
chris: create ticket and assign to eng-platform and devex to patch UI and add automated test. Also add audit instrumentation on the client click so we record attempted privileged UI actions (even if backend 403).
anya: for immediate workaround can we disable the Create button by default for viewers via a feature-flag?
kevin: I pushed a quick flag to prod: `feature.ui.strictRoleChecks=true` (rolled to 20% users). deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout/feature-ui-strict-2026-03-20 by kevin.
sec-bot: [auto] Label: security-ui-exposure. Recommend follow-up: KMS audit correlation and vulnerability triage meeting.
sara: next steps I will: 1) PR to clear cachedRoles on org switch (eng-platform) 2) Add e2e to assert button hidden for viewer 3) Add client click tracking event (devex) 4) Request KMS audit team to confirm no key access occurred (kevin).
chris: thanks — set target: patch in 48h, rollback/flag if any regression. Assigning owners: sara (UI patch), kevin (audit/KMS), anya (QA repro & screenshots).
anya: confirmed after 5m that the feature-flag rollout hides the button. leaving screenshots in the ticket. :thumbsup:
kevin: I'll also add an audit rule to alert if UI click occurs without matching audit entry within 1 minute — to catch dropped events.
sec-bot: [auto] Added to security backlog: RBAC-client-cache-eviction (#SEC-4893).
chris: thank you all. capture notes in the postmortem if this surfaces in more orgs.
anya: ok closing here after patch lands.
